    "design_critique": "1. Sensor footprints do not overlap. At 0.02 m pitch with 16 mm (0.016 m) footprints, each sensor leaves a 4 mm gap to its neighbour. The rationale says the footprints overlap, which is wrong. The 25 mm tape still spans at least one footprint at every offset (25 mm > 20 mm pitch), so the coverage claim holds. But the reading is not monotonic across the gaps, so the centroid signal can jump as the tape crosses a gap. This should be stated, and the 0.016 m footprint versus 0.012 m alternative should be justified against it.

2. The steering scale drops, and the rationale hides this. Weights of 33*x over x = -0.06 to +0.06 give a signal slope of about 33 per metre. Iteration 4 had about 40 per metre (weights +/-2 at +/-0.05 m, and +/-1 at +/-0.025 m), and iteration 2 had about 50. Effective proportional gain per cm is therefore kp*0.33 = 1.49 with kp 4.5, against 1.6 in iteration 4 and 2.0 in iteration 2. The draft says kp 4.5 keeps authority 'similar to iteration 4', which is roughly true, but it does not say the slope fell. Because ki and kd were not rescaled, the balance between proportional, integral and derivative action has also changed. That matters if the next race is read as a gain test.

3. Oscillation rose in the last race and the draft ignores it. Iteration 4 oval steering_oscillation was 0.28 (iterations 0 to 3 were about 0.07 to 0.16), and control_effort was 10.4 against about 3.8 before. The move to y = 0.07 may have caused this, as earlier sensing lets the loop overshoot. The draft raises kp to 4.5 and keeps kd at 0.6, so it adds proportional gain to a loop that was already oscillating more. The critique has to ask whether kp should go up at all before the oscillation is explained.

4. The geometry-is-the-limit claim is confounded. Iteration 4 changed sensor position, sensor span, footprint size and base_speed (0.9 to 1.0) together. The rationale calls the result 'sensing geometry is the main limit' without separating the effects. The speed change is small, so geometry is the more likely cause, but it is not isolated.

5. The failure mechanism is not established. Max_error sits at 0.061 to 0.062 on every track and every gain set, and progress is nearly identical across speeds 0.9 to 1.6 in iterations 0 to 3. That pattern suggests a fixed spatial or start-up failure, which the draft's own prior critique flagged. The draft changes sensing again without a test that locates the exit point (first bend, start, or a specific curvature).

6. Speed 1.0 is maintained without a completion plan. Oval completions at 1.0 came from a shorter track. The s-bend and slalom have no completions at any speed tested, so 1.0 cannot be justified as the completion speed on those tracks. The held-out track will be different, so the final design needs a speed that can finish in 3 s, which is about 1.5 m/s average. This draft does not move toward that and gives no plan to test it.

7. The 7-sensor span of +/-0.06 m is wider than the 0.06 m off-track limit. The outer sensors can read the tape only when the robot is already close to leaving, so they add little beyond the central sensors at the normal offset. Their value depends on whether the robot reaches the limit, which the evidence says it does at the same point each time.",
